work.title: Five Novels of the 1960s and 70s
work.first_publication: Library of America, 2008 (edited by Jonathan Lethem)

reading.synopsis: This is the second of two Library of America volumes dedicated to Philip K. Dick (following Four Novels of the 1960s, 2007), collecting Martian Time-Slip, Dr. Bloodmoney, Now Wait for Last Year, Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said, and A Scanner Darkly, and edited by Jonathan Lethem. Together the two Library of America volumes mark Dick's formal canonization into the American literary tradition, a status few science fiction writers of his generation achieved.
motifs: Institutional literary canonization of a writer who spent most of his career in the pulp genre marketplace
A curated span of Dick's most theologically and politically mature period (1964-1977) presented as a coherent artistic arc
reading.significance: Dick's inclusion in the Library of America -- an institution otherwise reserved for canonical figures of American letters -- represents one of the clearest institutional confirmations of his posthumous critical reassessment from genre pulp writer to major American novelist. Jonathan Lethem's editorial involvement across both Library of America volumes situates Dick within a lineage Lethem has championed in his own fiction and criticism.
reading.closing_note: This entry documents the omnibus as a publishing and canonization milestone; readers seeking analysis of the individual novels should consult each title's own dedicated dossier.
